newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber steady, new TSR20 contract debuts.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber steady, new TSR20 contract debuts.

text.p: Rubber futures finished steady on Friday while the debut of the new TSR20 contract which came into effect today was greeted quietly, dealers said.
The change in the TSR20 contract meant that transactions in the October/December 1997 contract would now use U.S. dollars instead of the previous Singapore dollars.
"The reception was not exceptional," one rubber trader said.

"About 240 tonnes was done in the new contract at around 129 U.S. cents a kg. But the debut was fairly quiet," a trader said. The Singapore Commodity Exchange (SICOM) said it was too early to make an assessment on the reception for the new TSR20
"We believe it will take about six months to gauge the effectivity of the new contract," a SICOM official said.
On other futures contracts, prices held largely steady on the back of mild shortcovering, traders said. "There was some buying, although it was not particularly heavy," one rubber dealer said.
December RSS3 was seen at 126.25-126.50 U.S. cents a kg at around 0945 GMT from the previous 126.50 cents.
